team.technicalDepth: Strong – all three founders have deep technical backgrounds in quantitative trading and large-scale engineering at top-tier tech companies.

product.plainLanguage: An AI agent platform that automates end-to-end tasks and workflows for small and mid-sized businesses, positioning itself as an 'AI Microsoft Office' for SMBs.

market.sizeHint: Large – the global SMB market comprises millions of businesses; the AI agent layer for SMBs is a nascent but rapidly expanding category.
market.competitiveLandscape: Horizontal AI assistants (Microsoft Copilot, Google Duet), vertical SaaS tools with AI features, and other AI agent startups targeting SMBs.
market.whyNow: LLM cost collapse and capability improvements make it feasible to deploy affordable, autonomous AI agents for resource-constrained SMBs.

risks.text: Dependence on third-party LLM providers for core model capabilities; margin pressure if model costs rise or access changes.
Intense competition from well-funded horizontal platforms (Microsoft, Google) that can bundle AI agents into existing SMB productivity suites.
SMB churn and price sensitivity may limit lifetime value and make customer acquisition economics challenging.
Execution risk in building a truly autonomous agent (vs. copilot) that reliably handles diverse SMB workflows without heavy customization.

scoreRationale: Motion scores well overall due to a technically exceptional team, a timely market entry with a clear AI-agent wedge, and fresh Series C traction. Defensibility is the main gap – the moat will depend on execution speed to build workflow lock-in before horizontal incumbents embed similar agents. Product clarity and market timing are strong.
